question_text: These parallel box plots show the weights of particular species of fungi collected from 3 different sites in a forest.

subparts.stem: Write down the five-number summary for site 1.

mark_breakdown.desc: All five values correctly read from the box plot for site 1

subparts.solution:
From the box plot for site 1:
$$\text{minimum} = 15, \quad Q_1 = 30, \quad \text{median} = 50, \quad Q_3 = 60, \quad \text{maximum} = 70$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Read the key points of the boxplot: lower whisker tip (min), left box edge ($Q_1$), central line (median), right box edge ($Q_3$), and upper whisker tip (max).
step_by_step: Left edge of box is at 30.
Right edge of box is at 60.

subparts.stem: Which site has the greatest range of weights?
subparts.solution: Site 3 has the greatest overall spread from whisker to whisker, hence Site 3 has the greatest range of weights.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The range is represented by the total span from the bottom whisker tip to the top whisker tip.
step_by_step: Check the total vertical span for Site 1, Site 2, and Site 3.
Site 3 extends over the largest vertical distance, so it has the greatest range.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Looking only at the length of the box (IQR) rather than the entire plot span.

subparts.stem: At which site do the weights of fungi have the least variation?
subparts.solution: The weights of fungi have the least variation at site 2, as it has the smallest overall span and smallest box length.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Variation is measured by spread (range or IQR); the smallest spread corresponds to the least variation.
step_by_step: Site 2 has both the shortest total length and the shortest box.
Thus, site 2 has the least variation.

subparts.stem: Which site has the highest median weight of fungi?
subparts.solution: Site 1 has the highest median weight of fungi (median = 50 g).

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Compare the positions of the horizontal lines indicating the median in each box.
step_by_step: Site 2 and Site 3 have medians below 50.
Therefore, Site 1 has the highest median.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Looking at the maximum rather than the median.

subparts.stem: Which site has the highest proportion of weights above 40 grams?
subparts.solution: Site 1 has the highest proportion of weights above 40 grams (around 75% are above 30, and the median is 50, meaning over 50% are above 50 g).

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Quartiles split the data into 25% sections. Determine the fraction of data lying above 40 grams for each site.
step_by_step: For Site 1, $Q_1 = 30$ and median $= 50$, so more than 50% of the distribution lies above 40 g.
For Sites 2 and 3, 40 g is at or above the median/upper quartile, meaning a smaller proportion is above 40 g.
Hence, Site 1 has the highest proportion above 40 g.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Comparing absolute numbers rather than proportions.
